textRuns.value: I loaded the six supplied CSV files using Power Query. Identified and removed one verified identical duplicate (EXP-0021), reducing the fact_exposure dataset from 49 to 48 records. Standardized text fields and currency codes, and converted text-formatted monetary values into numeric types.

One exposure (EXP-0011) has missing RWA and CapitalRequirement values. These were retained as blanks and flagged rather than estimated. Counterparty CP011 is absent from the master data, so a provisional dimension record named "Unknown counterparty" was added using the Poland country code shown in the source fact_exposure.

Implemented a star schema with five dimensions, a daily 2026 date table, and single-direction relationships to Fact_Exposure. All monetary values were treated as EUR, with no further currency conversion as mentioned in additional requirement at point # 3. Capital requirement includes an additional 2.5% of RWA buffer in the separately defined buffer measure. The original Capital Requirement % calculation remains unchanged.

Actual and Budget measures override scenario selection for comparison. Variances remain blank where either scenario is unavailable. The rolling three-month average uses only months containing Actual RWA data as required.

Implemented dynamic Country Manager RLS through user-to-country mappings and a separate unrestricted Group Viewer role. Validation is performed using the supplied test users and Power BI Desktop's View as feature, with Service-level testing required before production use.

The February Actual RWA is incomplete because of one missing value, affecting related KPIs and variances. CP011 has incomplete master data. The provided dataset contains only a limited set of reporting months, and the security emails provided are just sample for the the demonstration.

For production, I would collaborate closely with the Data Engineering team to ensure that data validation, exception logging, source reconciliation, and counterparty master data management are handled upstream.

From my side as a Power BI Developer, I would focus on building a governed, reusable semantic model, implementing appropriate RLS and managing access through security groups. I would use Git integration with Azure DevOps for version control and Power BI/Fabric deployment pipelines to promote changes across Development, Test, and Production environments.
I would also evaluate incremental refresh and model optimization based on data volume and performance requirements to ensure a reliable, secure, and maintainable reporting solution.
